Monisha compares f(x) = |x| and g(x) = |2x - 4|. She says g is f translated 4 right and compressed horizontally by 2. What is her error?

|2x - 4| = 2|x - 2|, so g is f translated 2 right and stretched vertically by 2 (or, read as f(2(x - 2)), compressed horizontally by 1/2 and shifted 2 right). Students must factor inside the absolute value before reading the transformations; the same inside-vs-outside reasoning as quiz item 1's choice D vs E.
The graph of f(x) = |x| is shown. Students graph g(x) = |x + c| for several values of c from -5 to 5.
A. Graph g(x) = |x + c| several times with different values of c (any value from -5 to 5).
B. Look for Relationships: predict what happens to the graph if c is greater than 100. What if c is between 0 and 1/2? (Very large shift left; very small shift left.)
What does the graph tell you about the range of f(x) = |x|? → The range is greater than or equal to zero.
What can you predict about the range of g(x) = |x + c| for different values of c? → Whatever c is, the range is still greater than or equal to zero.
How can you find points to graph for each function? → Make a table of values for x from -5 to 5 and compute y.
What do you notice about the vertex of each function? → The vertices all lie on the x-axis.
How does the graph change if the coefficient of f(x + c) is negative? Graph -f(x + c) for three of your functions. → The graphs of -f(x + c) are reflections of f(x + c) across the x-axis.
If f(x) has a horizontal shift, what part of the function has been changed? → x stands for the domain, so the operation is applied to x inside the parentheses.
If f(x) has a vertical shift, what part of the function has been changed? → f(x) stands for the range, so the operation is applied to f(x).
What happens to the graph if c is a negative number? → The graph shifts to the right when c is negative.
